references.text: Moses' account of blessings and curses, which includes warnings about the loss of land and national privileges, resembles Jesus' warning that God's kingdom will be taken from them and given to a people who produce its fruits.
Daniel prophesies about a new covenant and an eternal kingdom, suggesting the transfer of God's kingdom to a people who will bear its fruits.

Jesus' conversation with a Roman officer about faith, and his subsequent comment that many will come from east and west into God's kingdom while the children of Israel are cast out, parallels the idea that the kingdom will be taken from them and given to a people who produce its fruits.

The parable of the vineyard, where the tenants kill the son of the vineyard owner, and therefore the vineyard will be taken from them and given to others, is a direct parallel to Jesus' warning in Matthew 21:43.

Paul and Barnabas' declaration to the Jews that since they reject the gospel, they have judged themselves unworthy of eternal life, and therefore the gospel will be taken to the Gentiles, reflects the idea that God's kingdom will be taken from one people and given to another.
Paul's statement that God's salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen, emphasizes the transfer of God's kingdom to a people who will bear its fruits.
